features.name: useGraphData stable references (fix React #185 infinite topology loop)
features.behavior: Every function returned by useGraphData (createNode, updateNode, deleteNode, createEdge, updateEdge, deleteEdge, search, getTopology, exportGraph, importGraph) is wrapped in useCallback with correct deps, and the whole returned object is wrapped in useMemo, so consumers can safely put these functions in their own effect dependency arrays without retriggering on every render. Fixes a real production crash: toggling the topology overlay threw React error #185 ("Maximum update depth exceeded") because getTopology was a brand-new function literal on every render, and AppPage's topology useEffect had getTopology in its dependency array - each render the effect triggered created a new getTopology reference, which retriggered the effect, in an infinite loop; the effect's own .catch() swallowed the resulting failure and surfaced it as a misleading "Không tính được topology" alert instead of an obvious crash.
features.verification: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/hooks/useGraphData.test.js src/pages/AppPage.test.jsx
features.evidence: Reported 2026-08-25 via a real-usage bug report (importing a VESTA progress-graph JSON). Verified the root cause directly in useGraphData.js before fixing (getTopology defined inline in the returned object literal, no memoization). Added a referential-stability regression test (useGraphData.test.js) and a full end-to-end integration regression test (AppPage.test.jsx, 'toggling topology does not enter an infinite update loop') that clicks the real 'Độ quan trọng' button through the real (non-mocked) useGraphData hook. Confirmed the integration test is a genuine regression test, not a false positive: ran it against the pre-fix useGraphData.js (via git stash) and it failed (the topology button disappeared from the DOM, consistent with the reported crash); ran it again against the fix and it passed. Full frontend suite after fix: npm run test -> 15 files, 90 passed (up from 14 files/80 passed). npm run build -> 611 modules, clean. npm run lint -> oxlint 0 warnings/0 errors, 40 files.

features.name: Mock-mode cluster recompute on structural graph changes
features.behavior: New frontend/src/clustering/mockClustering.js computes connected-component clusters ({cluster_id, node_ids}, same shape as the real backend's Louvain-based ClusterService). useGraphData's mock-mode createNode/deleteNode/createEdge/deleteEdge/importGraph now call this after any structural change (node/edge added or removed) and update the `clusters` state accordingly, instead of leaving `clusters` frozen on the hardcoded mockData.js demo clusters forever. Deliberately NOT recomputed on every nodes/edges change via a passive effect, and NOT recomputed on updateNode/updateEdge (field edits don't change graph topology) - see Decisions.md for why (the bundled demo graph is a fully-connected star that would collapse into one cluster under naive connected-components on every render).
features.verification: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/clustering/mockClustering.test.js src/hooks/useGraphData.test.js
features.evidence: Reported 2026-08-25 alongside FE017 via the same VESTA-import bug report: importing a real 28-node/29-edge graph in mock mode rendered zero cluster hulls, because GraphCanvas.jsx's hullPathFor() looks up cluster.node_ids against ids that only exist in the hardcoded mockClusters ('p', 'c1', ...), which imported nodes (fresh crypto.randomUUID() ids) never match. Added mockClustering.test.js (6 tests: connected grouping, singleton isolation, disconnected components, dangling-edge tolerance, empty graph, partition invariant) and useGraphData.test.js regression tests asserting every current node id appears in exactly one cluster after importGraph/createNode/deleteNode. npm run test -> 15 files, 90 passed. npm run build -> 611 modules, clean. npm run lint -> 0/0, 40 files.

features.name: Universe visual theme system (starfield background, orbit motifs, space color tokens)
features.behavior: New base theme layer implemented: theme.js extended with universe-theme tokens (nebula[] gradient tints, orbitLine, starColor/starOpacityMin/Max, glow(color, strength) helper, cometDashArray) plus a deterministic seededRandom() helper - all existing tokens (canvasBg, panelBg, panelBorder, accent, depthColors, clusterPalette, etc.) kept as the same keys so every existing consumer (TopBar, GraphCanvas, all forms/pages) picks up the deepened space-black palette with zero code changes on their end. New Starfield.jsx component: canvas-based twinkling starfield (two depth layers for parallax-of-scale), CSS radial-gradient nebula glows, and SVG orbit-ring ellipses, mounted globally in App.jsx behind all routes. Respects prefers-reduced-motion (renders stars at fixed mid-brightness instead of animating). LandingPage's own opaque background removed so the global starfield shows through as the first visible use of the theme; AppPage's dense UI panels remain opaque over it by design. Foundational for FE023 (personalization), FE024 (marketing pages), and FE025 (3D graph), which all build their look on these same tokens/component.

features.name: 3D graph view with 2D/3D toggle button
features.behavior: New GraphCanvas3D.jsx renders nodes as glowing spheres and edges as lines in a three.js WebGL scene, with OrbitControls camera (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom) matching the universe theme (FE022). Node positions come from a new pure-JS module, graph3d/computeLayout.js: a 3D force-directed simulation (pairwise repulsion + edge springs + gentle centering, seeded deterministically via theme.seededRandom) computed once via useMemo when nodes/edges change - the render loop itself only does camera/rendering work, never physics. A new segmented 2D/3D toggle in TopBar.jsx (viewMode/onViewModeChange props, new topbar.view_2d/view_3d locale keys in all 3 languages) switches AppPage between the existing 2D GraphCanvas and the new 3D view. Click-to-select (via raycasting, with a small drag-distance threshold to distinguish clicks from camera-orbit drags) and cluster-based node coloring (using the same theme.clusterPalette as the 2D hull overlay) are supported. Scoped out of v1, tracked as a known gap rather than silently dropped: topology-based node sizing and search highlight/match-dimming (both present in the 2D view) are not yet implemented in 3D. GraphCanvas3D is lazy-loaded via React.lazy()/Suspense so three.js (~540kB minified) only downloads the first time a user actually opens the 3D view, keeping the main bundle size unaffected for users who never switch. No backend change required - 3D positions are computed entirely client-side from the same /nodes and /edges data the 2D view already consumes (see F023 for the optional future persistence extension).
features.verification: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/graph3d/computeLayout.test.js src/components/GraphCanvas3D.test.jsx src/pages/AppPage.test.jsx
features.evidence: 2026-08-25. Implemented per the universe-theme roadmap. Installed three.js (0.185.1) and used its bundled OrbitControls addon rather than hand-rolling camera controls. Validated the 3D force layout algorithm numerically BEFORE writing any rendering code (checked for NaN/Infinity, determinism, and the key correctness property that directly-connected nodes end up closer together than nodes in a separate component) - this caught nothing wrong, but confirmed the algorithm was sound before building the harder-to-test rendering layer on top of it. computeLayout.test.js (7 tests): empty graph, single node (no NaN), moderately-connected 15-node graph (no NaN/Infinity anywhere), determinism across calls, connected-closer-than-disconnected property, dangling-edge tolerance, full node coverage with no duplicates. GraphCanvas3D.test.jsx (6 tests): mounts/unmounts cleanly even with jsdom's real getContext('webgl') returning null (three.js's WebGLRenderer throws 'Error creating WebGL context' in that case - caught by a try/catch mirroring Starfield.jsx's null-2d-context handling), renders with an empty graph, renders with clusters provided, re-renders without throwing when nodes/edges change, tolerates a dangling edge referencing a nonexistent node id. AppPage.test.jsx: new integration test clicking the real '3D'/'2D' toggle buttons and confirming the correct canvas component is mounted at each state (awaiting the Suspense boundary's lazy import to resolve). Caught and fixed a real bundle-size regression mid-session: the initial (non-lazy) import of GraphCanvas3D more than doubled the production bundle (340kB -> 885kB minified) because three.js loaded unconditionally for every user, even ones who never open the 3D view. Fixed via React.lazy()/Suspense - confirmed via a second build that the main bundle returned to 341kB with three.js split into its own 543kB-only-loaded-on-demand chunk. Full verification: npm run test -> 21 files, 131 passed (up from 117 before this session). npm run build -> 624 modules, clean, correct code-split chunks. npm run lint -> 0 warnings/0 errors, 53 files. Backend re-confirmed unaffected: pytest -q -> 129 passed, 1 skipped (unchanged).

features.name: Gate authenticated app to live data only; mock lives exclusively on marketing pages
features.behavior: New frontend/src/config/env.js exports IS_DEV (import.meta.env.DEV), centralizing the dev/production check behind one small, easily-mockable module rather than reading import.meta.env.DEV directly at every call site. AppPage.jsx's default source state is now IS_DEV ? 'mock' : 'live' (was always 'mock') - a real production build defaults to live data on mount, not the mock demo. TopBar.jsx's Mock/Live toggle buttons are now rendered only when IS_DEV is true - completely absent from a production build (and, as a bonus of Vite's dead-code elimination on the build-time-substituted import.meta.env.DEV literal, the toggle's JSX doesn't even ship in the production bundle). The mock demo experience now lives exclusively on the public marketing pages (FE024's Example section) - a real logged-in user in production can no longer switch their actual project view to placeholder data at all. In dev/test builds (IS_DEV=true, which is Vitest's and `npm run dev`'s default), behavior is completely unchanged: source still defaults to 'mock' and the toggle still renders, so local development/testing never requires a live backend and zero pre-existing tests needed to change.
